children: There are good reasons to believe that Australia's current housing market downturn is different to the garden variety cyclical downswings of recent decades, says Paul Bloxham, chief economist for Australia at HSBC. The decline so far is already bigger and sharper than the previous ones, while core inflation remains elevated, despite aggressive interest rate increases this year, he adds. Near-term interest rate cuts are not on the agenda while tax changes and the likelihood that global rates will stay high for longer are adding to the grim picture. Bloxham expects a 13% peak-to-trough house price fall. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
